what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/ask-questions-sort-answers-follow-up: make quiz questions, check a form's answers, score answers into a segment (listed from records.json), and keep forms, answers and decisions as rows in the person's own Postgres with plain SQL.

payload.label: Questions and answers: quiz questions from text, checking form answers, scoring answers into segments
Make a form record
payload.job: Check a form, a list of questions people answer, and keep it in the person's own database, so it can be asked and its answers checked
payload.description: Give a form_id, an optional title and presentation, and the questions. Each question needs a questionId and a questionTypeId (a row in the question-type list: text, long text, number, rating, choice, a reference to a file) and may carry a label, required, options, its own validation rules laid over its type's, and an afterSaved hand-off naming an owner and an action. The form is kept as one row of the table question_sequence (the same form_id replaces the same row) and answered with how many questions it holds. It reaches no database: it answers the row to keep as keep.

form_id.description: The form's name, kept in the record id

presentation.description: How the form is shown: a mode and the words of its Back, Next and Submit buttons

record.description: The question-sequence row kept: id, type and value

keep.description: The rows this call made, {id, type, value}, for the caller to keep in the person's own database

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/ask-questions-sort-answers-follow-up (its record builders and readers); the tools keep their rows in the person's own Postgres with plain SQL

payload.label: Check and decide form answers
payload.job: Check a person's answers against a form kept in the database and, when they are all valid, keep them with the score and segment they earn and any follow-up the form hands to its owner
payload.description: Give form_id, respondent_id and answers (questionId to value). The form is read from the table question_sequence (make it with save-a-form) and the rules that decide the segment from the tables score_rule, segment_rule and follow_up_sequence. Optionally submission_id (for a form answered again and again, so each time has its own rows) and answered_at. The answers are checked against the form as check-form-answers does. If any is invalid the first to fix is returned and nothing is kept. Otherwise one transaction keeps an answer fact for each answer the form asks about (table answer_fact), one segment assignment (segment_assignment) and one request row for each question whose afterSaved names an owner and action, with the answers filled into its input (owner_action_request), and the tool answers the decision (score and segment), the segment's follow-up sequence and the rows kept. It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows, and keep the rows the answer lists in keep.

respondent_id.description: Who is answering; answers of one respondent group together

answers.description: Each question's answer, keyed by questionId

submission_id.description: Names this time of answering, so a repeated form keeps every time

rows.description: The person's form rows this call reads ({id, type, value}, type the row's kind: question-sequence, answer-fact, segment-assignment, score-rule, segment-rule, follow-up-sequence), read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them

records.description: The rows the answers made and kept: answer facts, the segment assignment, owner action requests

keep.description: The rows this call made, {id, type, value}, for the caller to keep in the person's own database

payload.label: Form results
payload.job: Show who answered a form, the score each earned and the segment each was sorted into, with a count per segment, from the segment assignments in the database
payload.description: Give optionally a form_id to see one form, or nothing to see every form in the table segment_assignment. Returns rows (respondentId, formId, segmentId, score, decidedAt), newest decision first, and a summary with the total and a count per segment. No assignments gives an empty list, never an invented one. It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows.

payload.label: Answers over time
payload.job: Show one person's answers to a form across every time they answered, in order, and the trend of one numeric answer, from the answer facts in the database
payload.description: Give form_id, respondent_id and field_map (the name you want for each answer, to its questionId), and optionally trend_field (which mapped answer to chart; default the first that is numeric). The answer facts are read from the table answer_fact. Returns one row per time answered, oldest first, with the mapped answers and when; the numeric series for the trend; the latest row; and the count. A person who has not answered gets no rows. It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows.

payload.label: Latest answers as lines
payload.job: Give the latest answers to a form as plain lines, each starting with the question it answers, ready to hand to a writer or a summary, from the database
payload.description: Give form_id and optionally respondent_id. The form is read from the table question_sequence and its answers from answer_fact. Returns lines: the most recent time the form was answered, one "Question: answer" line per non-empty answer (the bare answer when the question's label is not known). It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows.

payload.label: Read a form page
payload.job: Read one live form page: its words, how many questions it asks and where a visitor's answers are kept
payload.description: Answers the form page named by page from the pursuit database form_rows: its title, its plain words, the number of questions its form asks and the site whose sign-in keeps a visitor's answers. A page that is not live, is unknown or names a form with no questions is refused in the page row's own words. The answer is the props of show/FormPageScreen.tsx.

database.description: The name of the pursuit database to read, bound by the trusted caller. The engine opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection; no caller supplies a login.

use.description: The use this statement runs for: a recipe step's declared purpose and surface (config.context.use, set by the workflow engine over any use the step's input carried). Given with database, the computer opens the database with its reader login (one that cannot get round the row rules, change a table or read the use binding) instead of the owner's, and hands the run a ticket of this use that it signed; the statement's transaction claims it first, so the database's row rules read this use and the statement cannot change it. A use with credential_name, which has no ticket, is refused. Absent: the owner's own work, read under the database's own purpose_when_unstated.

purpose.description: The purpose path, such as publish or coach/review.

surface.description: The surface path, such as social/instagram; empty for any surface.

page.description: The form page's name; its row is form-page:<page>.

payload.label: Start a form sitting
payload.job: Start one person's go at a form page, one question at a time
payload.description: Opens a sitting of the form page named by page and answers its id (attemptId) and the first step to draw. With person the sitting is that signed-in member's; without it the sitting is the visitor's own until it is kept. A page that is not live is refused by name.

person.description: The signed-in member's email, named by the trusted caller (the page's own sign-in); never chosen by a browser or an AI's arguments.

use.description: The use this step runs for (a site's declared pages use, or a recipe step's config.context.use). Given with database, the computer opens the database with its writer login (one that may add or change only the columns the writer recipe may-write-named-columns-under-a-use named, and never change a table) instead of the owner's, and hands the run a ticket of this use that it signed; the step's one transaction claims it first. A share act's run must give it. Absent: the owner's own work, with the owner's login.

payload.label: Answer a form question
payload.job: Keep one answer of a form page sitting and say the next step
payload.description: Checks the value as the sitting's waiting question asks it, keeps it as that question's answer (answering the same question again replaces it) and answers the next step to draw. A value that fails the question's rule is refused by naming the rule, never the value. A sitting already kept is refused.

payload.label: Keep a form sitting
payload.job: Keep a form page sitting's answers under the email the sign-in proved
payload.description: Moves the sitting's answers to the person named by person and writes the decision the form's rules make (the segment and any follow-up requests), all together, then marks the sitting kept. Keeping again under the same person answers the same; a sitting kept by someone else is refused. Without person nothing is kept.
